text:
Must-Know SQL Differences Every Developer Should Know

🔹 RANK() vs DENSE_RANK() vs ROW_NUMBER()
ROW_NUMBER() → unique number per row (no ties)
RANK() → same rank for ties, skips numbers
DENSE_RANK() → same rank for ties, no gaps
👉 Use ROW_NUMBER for deduplication
 👉 Use DENSE_RANK for leaderboards

🔹 WHERE vs HAVING
WHERE filters rows before aggregation
HAVING filters after aggregation
👉 Aggregates belong in HAVING, not WHERE

🔹 UNION vs UNION ALL
UNION removes duplicates (extra sort cost)
UNION ALL keeps duplicates (faster)
👉 Default to UNION ALL unless deduplication is required

🔹 INNER JOIN vs LEFT JOIN
INNER JOIN returns only matching rows
LEFT JOIN keeps all left records
👉 Use INNER JOIN when nulls are not needed for better performance

🔹 COUNT(*) vs COUNT(column)
COUNT(*) counts all rows
COUNT(column) ignores NULLs
👉 Critical for accurate metrics

🔹 NOT IN vs NOT EXISTS
NOT IN breaks when NULL exists
NOT EXISTS is NULL-safe
👉 Always prefer NOT EXISTS

🔹 BETWEEN vs >= and <=
BETWEEN is inclusive on both ends
Can cause boundary bugs with dates
👉 Be explicit for date filters


💡 SQL doesn’t fail loudly.
 It fails quietly with wrong results.

author: Divya Gudikandula
headline: Data Analyst | Power BI | SQL | DAX | SSIS | 10+ Years IT Experience | Open to Work
text:
🔍 SQL Interview Question:
How to get the 2nd Highest Salary in SQL – Multiple ways

Assume table EMPLOYEE(id, name, salary)
1 . Using MAX() with Subquery (Most Common)

 1 )SELECT MAX(salary) AS second_highest_salary
FROM employee
WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employee);
✔ Simple & frequently asked
⚠️ Returns NULL if only one distinct salary exists


2 )Using ROW_NUMBER()

SELECT salary
FROM (
 SELECT salary,
 ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rn
 FROM employee
) t
WHERE rn = 2;
⚠️ May fail with duplicate salaries

3 )Using DENSE_RANK() (Best Practice ⭐)

SELECT salary
FROM (
 SELECT salary,
 DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rnk
 FROM employee
) t
WHERE rnk = 2;
✔ Handles duplicate salaries correctly
✔ Most recommended for real-world queries

4 )Using OFFSET FETCH (ANSI Standard)

SELECT DISTINCT salary
FROM employee
ORDER BY salary DESC
OFFSET 1 ROW FETCH NEXT 1 ROW ONLY;
✔ Supported in modern Oracle, SQL Server, PostgreSQL

Learn how to slice data with conditions, using operators like BETWEEN, IN, and logical operators like AND, OR, and NOT. Mastering these will allow you to extract meaningful insights from large datasets.

🔗 𝗝𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘀 –
Understand how to combine data from multiple tables using INNER, LEFT, RIGHT, and FULL OUTER joins. Joining tables is critical when working with normalised databases, and knowing how to use these joins effectively can drastically improve your data analysis.

📊 𝗪𝗶𝗻𝗱𝗼𝘄 𝗙𝘂𝗻𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 –
Use advanced functions like RANK(), LEAD(), LAG(), and ROW_NUMBER() for advanced analytics. These powerful tools allow you to perform calculations over a specific range of rows without collapsing the data, which is invaluable for tasks like running totals, ranking, and time-series analysis.

📅 𝗗𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗙𝘂𝗻𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 –
Work with time-based data using functions like DATE_TRUNC(), EXTRACT(), NOW(), and more. Date manipulation is a must-have skill when analysing time-series data or performing time-based aggregations.

📈 𝗔𝗱𝘃𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲𝗱 𝗔𝗻𝗮𝗹𝘆𝘁𝗶𝗰𝘀 –

🔄 𝗖𝗧𝗘𝘀, 𝗧𝗲𝗺𝗽 𝗧𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲𝘀 & 𝗦𝘂𝗯𝗾𝘂𝗲𝗿𝗶𝗲𝘀 –
Reusing logic with WITH clauses, recursive queries, and subqueries can make your queries more readable, maintainable, and performant. Unlock the power of modular SQL by breaking complex queries into simpler components.

⚡ 𝗣𝗲𝗿𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝗢𝗽𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗶𝘇𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 –
Learn how to optimise your queries with indexing, query planning, and writing efficient queries for dashboards. This is a crucial skill for anyone dealing with large-scale datasets or real-time data.

text:
🚀 Snowflake + SQL Interview Prep: What You Must Know

If you are preparing for Data Engineer / Analyst interviews, these Snowflake SQL functions and questions show up a lot. Save this 🔖

👉 Common Snowflake SQL Functions

* QUALIFY – filter results after window functions
* ROW_NUMBER(), RANK(), DENSE_RANK() – ranking problems
* DATEADD(), DATEDIFF(), DATE_TRUNC() – date logic
* NVL(), COALESCE() – handle NULLs
* IFF() – Snowflake’s IF-ELSE
* TO_VARCHAR(), TO_NUMBER() – type casting
* ARRAY_AGG(), FLATTEN() – semi-structured data
* MERGE – upserts (very important)

👉 Frequently Asked SQL Interview Questions

* Difference between WHERE, HAVING, and QUALIFY
* Find 2nd / Nth highest salary
* Remove duplicates using SQL
* Window functions vs GROUP BY
* How MERGE works in Snowflake
* Clustering vs Partitioning
* How Snowflake handles scaling and performance
* Handling JSON data in Snowflake

👉 What to focus on!

Interviewers don’t just test syntax — they test:
✔️ problem-solving
✔️ performance thinking
✔️ real-world scenarios

If you can explain why you’re using a function, you’re already ahead 🙌
